newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China steel industry consolidating - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: China steel industry consolidating - Salomon.

text.p: China's steel industry growth will be stunted over the next few years as the sector consolidates, companies merge, and more steel firms list on Hong Kong's stock exchange, an investment bank report said on Monday.

"Over the next few years, smaller, loss-making plants are expected to merge with larger steel enterprises, product quality is likely to be lifted, product mix adjusted and more steel enterprises will be listed in Hong Kong," the Salomon Brothers report said.
The report said China's Wugang, Angang Sanxi, Panzhihua, Zhongqing Iron and Steel and Tianjin Steel Pipe were seeking listing approval.
In 1996, steel mills' profitability continued to decline, with the sector's total after-tax profit at three billion yuan ($362 million), down eight billion yuan from 1995, the report said.

Fixed asset investment in the steel sector in 1997 will be maintained at last year's level of 48 billion yuan, much lower than the 73.7 billion yuan demanded by the steel enterprises combined, the report said.
As a result of a planned economy, steel plants have set targets and run at full capacity, resulting in high inventory and accounts receivable, Salomon Brothers said.
Although China's total inventory was reduced from 26 million tonnes in 1995 to 23 million tonnes in 1996, cheaper imports from the CIS would make further reductions difficult, it said.

According to the Ministry of Metallurgy Industry (MMI), China spent US$42 billion between 1993 and 1996 on iron and steel imports, an amount larger than the accumulated investment in the industry over the past ten years, the report said.
China produced 34.34 million tonnes of steel in January to April this year, a 6.4 percent jump compared to the same period in 1996, the official China Daily said earlier this month.

"If we maintain the average daily output level of the first quarter, the annual output of steel will surpass 100 million tonnes," the newspaper quoted an official of the Ministry of Metallurgical industry as saying.
China aims to cut two million tonnes of imports by boosting domestic output of quality steel this year, officials have said.
